title: CNC drilling machine hydraulic requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Port-level repaired topology for a single-cycle open-circuit hydraulic drilling/clamping circuit. Tank.S supplies Pump.S; Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P and CycleDCV.P, with ReliefValve.T and all valve returns/drains connected directly to Tank.R. CycleDCV extend feeds the clamp cap through a non-compensated one-way meter-in flow control and a clamp cap pilot-operated check. Actual clamp cap-side pressure after the metering and holding elements pilots the externally piloted ForwardSequenceValve, whose selected catalog class is documented with integral free reverse A-to-P check flow and then enables the drill cap meter-in feed branch. CycleDCV retract feeds the drill rod only through a mechanically position-operated gate that closes at the drill-retracted condition, with a parallel plain check for drill rod exhaust during feed while blocking reverse powered supply during clamp release. Clamp release is supplied through an externally piloted ReturnSequenceValve, also documented with integral free reverse A-to-P check flow, whose pilot is vented until the drill-retracted position valve closes; its sequenced outlet supplies the clamp rod and pilots the clamp cap check open. No tees, manifolds, hoses, electrical interfaces, mechanical drive interfaces, shafts, or couplings are instantiated; repeated endpoints represent hydraulic branches.

function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank.S supplies Pump.S; Pump.P branches directly to CycleDCV.P and ReliefValve.P; ReliefValve.T and CycleDCV.T return directly to Tank.R. CycleDCV neutral unloads P to T while work ports are blocked, and ReliefValve limits maximum pressure.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: metered clamp extension with cap-side pilot check and mechanically conditioned sequenced release
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: CycleDCV extend sends metered flow through ClampAdvanceFlowControl A-B and ClampCapPilotCheck V-C to ClampCylinder.Cap. During clamp advance, ClampCylinder.Rod exhaust returns through the catalog-documented ReturnSequenceValve A-to-P reverse check to CycleDCV.B and tank. During drilling the pilot check blocks clamp cap exhaust. During release, ReturnSequenceValve opens only after the drill-retracted interlock permits pilot pressure; ReturnSequenceValve.A supplies ClampCylinder.Rod and pilots ClampCapPilotCheck.X open for clamp cap exhaust.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: externally piloted clamp-pressure sequence to drill meter-in feed with gated drill retract supply
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ForwardSequenceValve.X senses actual clamp cap-side pressure after clamp metering and holding elements. When it opens, ForwardSequenceValve.A supplies DrillFeedFlowControl A-B to meter flow into DrillCylinder.Cap. During retract, drill cap exhaust returns through DrillFeedFlowControl B-to-A reverse flow and the catalog-documented ForwardSequenceValve A-to-P reverse check to CycleDCV.A and tank. CycleDCV retract supplies DrillCylinder.Rod through DrillRetractPositionGate only until the drill-retracted trip closes the gate; DrillRodExhaustCheck permits rod exhaust during feed while blocking reverse powered supply during clamp release.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: externally piloted pressure sequence valve using actual clamp cap-side pressure with integral reverse check
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ForwardSequenceValve.P receives the CycleDCV.A extend supply, but its opening pilot X is connected to ClampCapPilotCheck.C, the clamp cap-side pressure point after clamp meter-in and holding elements. This prevents drill feed until the actual clamp pressure context is reached. The selected catalog state paths provide free reverse A-to-P flow in closed and open states, completing the drill cap exhaust path during drill retract without a separate bypass check.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: mechanical drill-retracted return interlock with pilot vent, rod-supply isolation, and integral reverse check
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: During drill retract, DrillRetractPositionGate is open and ReturnPilotVentPositionValve vents ReturnSequenceValve.X so clamp release is blocked. At the drill-retracted mechanical condition, the rod gate closes to remove powered drill rod supply and the pilot vent closes so ReturnSequenceValve.X can build pilot pressure. ReturnSequenceValve then opens P-A to feed ClampCylinder.Rod and pilot ClampCapPilotCheck.X. The selected catalog state paths provide free reverse A-to-P flow in closed and open states, completing the clamp rod exhaust path during clamp advance without a separate bypass check.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: main relief valve from pump pressure to tank
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ReliefValve opens from P to T at the pressure limit, returning excess pump flow directly to Tank.R and protecting the fixed-displacement pump circuit during stalls or end-of-stroke pressure rise.

assumptions: All components are generic hydraulic schematic components; pressure ratings, flow ratings, bore, rod, stroke, pump displacement, relief setting, and sequence settings are deferred to sizing.
The clamp advance and drill-feed advance loads are treated as resistive exactly as stated by the selected motion-control decisions; actuator orientation and gravity effects remain unresolved.
The selected one-way flow-control catalog class provides internal free reverse flow from B to A, so no duplicate bypass check is added around those speed controls.

The selected externally piloted sequence-valve catalog class provides internal free reverse flow from A to P in closed and open states, so no duplicate bypass checks are added around ForwardSequenceValve or ReturnSequenceValve.

The selected externally piloted sequence-valve phase states represent dominant operating intervals: closed before the relevant pilot condition is reached and open after the pilot condition is satisfied.

The selected position-operated bypass states are phase-level abstractions of the drill-retracted mechanical trip; the mechanical operator is a property of the selected generic class and is not represented as a separate component.
No electrical command wiring, solenoid interfaces, motor, coupling, shaft, tee, manifold, hose, filter, cooler, or gauge components are represented in this hydraulic topology.
open_issues: Cylinder bore, rod, stroke, pump flow, and valve settings remain sizing-phase tasks.
Actuator orientation remains unspecified; if later found to create overrunning motion, load-control topology must be revisited.
Mechanical placement of the drill-retracted position operators must be confirmed in machine integration; the position operator is a property of the selected position valve, not a separate component.
The non-electrical return interlock pattern is plausible and uses catalog position and sequence behavior, but machine-specific mechanical actuation placement should be validated before release.

research_coverage.summary: Most basic circuit patterns are supported: open hydraulic power unit with reservoir/pump/return/relief, 4/3 directional control of double-acting cylinders, meter-in advance for resistive clamp/drill feed, and pressure-sequence interlock so clamp pressure permits drill feed. However, the evidence is not yet sufficient for a safe final topology because the clamp load-holding requirement is only negatively/partially supported: current findings show tandem-center spool leakage can allow creep, but do not provide a positively supported leak-resistant clamp-holding topology such as pilot-operated check/load-holding valve placement and pilot release logic. The flow-control evidence also lacks the reverse-flow bypass/one-way flow-control detail needed to make advance meter-in compatible with unrestricted retract/release phases.

items.rationale: Findings provide cited connection logic for an open circuit: reservoir to pump inlet, pressure line to valves/loads, returns to reservoir, filtration, and a main relief branch from pressure line to tank. Technical evidence states fixed-displacement pump circuits require relief valves and open-center/all-ports-open neutral can unload pump flow.

Findings provide cited actuator and DCV pattern for a double-acting clamp cylinder controlled by a 4-way/3-position valve, including A-to-cap/B-to-rod convention and P→A/B→T extension, P→B/A→T retraction. Neutral behavior options are supported, including why all-ports-open floats and why tandem center alone is not reliable holding.

Meter-in clamp advance at cap-end supply is supported for resistive loads, and the pressure-sequence valve evidence supports automatic transition after clamping pressure rises. However, the findings explicitly lack evidence for a check-valve/reverse-flow bypass around the cap-end flow control, which is needed if clamp release/retract is intended to be unrestricted rather than throttled by the same meter-in restriction. The clamp-hold phase also depends on the unresolved leak-resistant holding topology.

The current evidence shows that all-ports-open neutral is unsuitable for holding and that tandem-center spool valves may creep due to leakage under outside forces, so it correctly warns against relying on DCV center alone. But it does not provide cited positive connection guidance for a leak-resistant clamp-holding component placed at the actuator, such as pilot-operated check valves or a hydraulic lock/load-holding valve, nor how it is released during clamp retract.

Findings support a double-acting drill-feed cylinder controlled by a 4-way/3-position directional valve with cited extend/retract port logic and neutral behavior choices. That is enough for directional-control topology; any load-holding issue is primarily associated with clamp and/or overrunning feed conditions.

Meter-in drill-feed advance at cap-end supply is supported for resistive loads, and retract without added regulation is plausible. But the findings lack cited evidence for one-way flow-control/check-bypass placement that would allow free reverse flow during retract if the advance meter-in valve remains in the cap-end line. Current sources also warn meter-in is unsafe for overrunning/assisting loads, so the designer must either confirm a resistive feed load or use the already-supported meter-out/counterbalance alternative.

Findings provide cited component and connection logic for a normally closed pressure sequence valve in the drill/feed branch so clamp flow occurs first; when clamp contact raises pressure above the setting, the valve opens to permit the secondary drill/feed function. Manufacturer evidence also supports port-level sequence-valve connections and piloted sequencing from another function.

The requirement is specifically leak-resistant clamp retention while drilling. Current evidence only establishes that DCV center conditions are insufficient or leakage-prone for dead-still holding; it does not yet cite the appropriate leak-resistant holding topology, actuator-port placement, or pilot-release path for unclamping. This is safety-critical and cannot be marked covered from negative evidence alone.

Findings support main relief protection for fixed-pump circuits and for actuator stall with DCV shifted, which covers the approximate 8 bar maximum-pressure topology. The pressure-sequence evidence supports a pressure-triggered transition to the drill/feed branch at a chosen setting, while also noting that the sequence valve is not a downstream pressure limiter and separate relief remains required for stall protection.

missing_or_weak_information: Missing positive, cited topology for leak-resistant clamp holding: exact component class, placement at/near clamp cylinder port(s), and pilot/release connection for unclamping.
Missing cited reverse-flow bypass/one-way flow-control guidance so cap-end meter-in advance does not unintentionally throttle clamp release or drill retract.
Potential machine-specific uncertainty remains whether drill-feed advance is purely resistive; current evidence says meter-in is unsuitable for assisting/overrunning loads.

design_issues.description: The non-electrical return interlock is functionally represented by drill-retracted position-operated valves that close the drill rod supply gate and close the return-sequence pilot vent before clamp release. This satisfies the intended topology at the schematic level, but the research did not provide detailed evidence for the exact mechanical actuation arrangement. Confirm the drill-retracted mechanical operator placement during machine integration.

CycleDCV is identified as a solenoid 4/3 DCV. The brief forbids electrical sensing/sequencing, not necessarily an electrically commanded cycle valve, and the actual sequencing is hydraulic/mechanical. If the intended constraint is later interpreted as no electrical devices at all, this valve actuation selection should be changed to a non-electrical actuation method without altering the hydraulic topology.

design_review.summary: The topology provides complete open-circuit supply, return, relief, extend/retract paths, cap-side meter-in feed controls, clamp-pressure drill enable, clamp holding during drilling, and a non-electrical drill-retracted interlock before clamp release. No blocking functional topology errors were found.
